{{short description|Probability multivariate distribution}}
{{Refimprove|date=April 2020}}
{{Probability distribution
  | box_width  = 350px
  | type       = mass
  | notation   = <math>\textrm{DNM}(x_0,\,\alpha_0 ,\, \boldsymbol{\alpha})</math>
  | parameters = <math> x_0 \in \R_{>0}, \alpha_0 \in \R_{>0}, \boldsymbol{\alpha} \in \R_{>0}^{m} </math>
 
  | support    = <math>x_i \in \{0,1,2,\ldots\}, 1\leq i\leq m</math>
  | pdf        = <math> \frac{\mathrm{B}(x_\bullet,\alpha_\bullet)}{\mathrm{B}(x_0,\alpha_0)}\prod_{i=1}^m \frac{\Gamma(x_i+\alpha_i)}{x_i!\Gamma(\alpha_i)} </math><br/> where <math> x_{\bullet}=\Sigma_{i=0}^{m}x_i </math> ,<math> \alpha_{\bullet}=\Sigma_{i=0}^{m}\alpha_i </math> and Γ(''x'') is the [[Gamma function]] and B is the [[beta function]].
  | cdf        =
  | mean       = <math> \tfrac{x_0}{\alpha_0-1}\boldsymbol{\alpha} </math>  for <math>\alpha_0>1</math>
  | variance   = <math> \,\frac{x_0(x_0+\alpha_0-1)}{(\alpha_0-1)^2(\alpha_0-2)}\left[\boldsymbol{\alpha} \boldsymbol{\alpha}^{\operatorname{T}} + (\alpha_0-1)\operatorname{diag}(\boldsymbol{\alpha}) \right] </math> for <math>\alpha_0>2</math>

  | mode       =
  | entropy    =
  | mgf        = does not exist
  | cf         = <math> \frac{\mathrm{B}(x_0, \alpha_{\bullet})}{\mathrm{B}(x_0,\alpha_0)} F_D^{(m)}(x_0,\boldsymbol{\alpha};x_0+\alpha_{\bullet}; e^{it_1}, \cdots,e^{it_m} ) </math> <br/> where  <math>F_D^{(m)}</math> is the [[Lauricella hypergeometric series|Lauricella function]] 
  }}

In [[probability theory]] and [[statistics]], the '''Dirichlet negative multinomial distribution''' is a [[Joint probability distribution|multivariate distribution]] on the non-negative integers. It is a multivariate extension of the [[beta negative binomial distribution]]. It is also a generalization of the [[negative multinomial distribution]] (NM(''k'',&thinsp;''p'')) allowing for heterogeneity or [[overdispersion]] to the [[probability vector]]. It is used in [[quantitative marketing research]] to flexibly model the number of household transactions across multiple brands.

If parameters of the [[Dirichlet distribution]] are <math>\boldsymbol{\alpha}</math>, and if
:<math>
X \mid p \sim \operatorname{NM}(x_0,\mathbf{p}),
</math>
where
:<math>
 \mathbf{p} \sim \operatorname{Dir}(\alpha_0,\boldsymbol\alpha),
</math>
then the marginal distribution of ''X'' is a Dirichlet negative multinomial distribution:
:<math>
X \sim \operatorname{DNM}(x_0,\alpha_0,\boldsymbol{\alpha}).
</math>

In the above, <math> \operatorname{NM}(x_0, \mathbf{p})</math> is the [[negative multinomial distribution]] and <math> \operatorname{Dir}(\alpha_0,\boldsymbol\alpha) </math> is the [[Dirichlet distribution]].


==Motivation==
===Dirichlet negative multinomial as a compound distribution===
The Dirichlet distribution is a [[conjugate distribution]] to the negative multinomial distribution. This fact leads to an analytically tractable [[compound distribution]].
For a random vector of category counts <math>\mathbf{x}=(x_1,\dots,x_m)</math>, distributed according to a [[negative multinomial distribution]], the compound distribution is obtained by integrating on the distribution for '''p''' which can be thought of as a [[random vector]] following a Dirichlet distribution:
 
:<math>\Pr(\mathbf{x}\mid x_0, \alpha_0, \boldsymbol{\alpha})=\int_{\mathbf{p}}\mathrm{NegMult}(\mathbf{x}\mid x_0, \mathbf{p}) \mathrm{Dir}(\mathbf{p}\mid\alpha_0,\boldsymbol{\alpha})\textrm{d}\mathbf{p}</math>

:<math>\Pr(\mathbf{x}\mid x_0, \alpha_0, \boldsymbol{\alpha})={\frac{\Gamma\left(\sum_{i=0}^m{x_i}\right)}{\Gamma(x_0)\prod_{i=1}^m x_i!}}  \frac{1}{\mathrm{B}(\boldsymbol\alpha_+)}\int_{\mathbf{p}} \prod_{i=0}^m p_i^{x_i+\alpha_i - 1}\textrm{d}\mathbf{p} </math>

which results in the following formula:

:<math>\Pr(\mathbf{x}\mid x_0, \alpha_0, \boldsymbol{\alpha})={\frac{\Gamma\left(\sum_{i=0}^m{x_i}\right)}{\Gamma(x_0)\prod_{i=1}^m x_i!}}  \frac{{\mathrm{B}}(\mathbf{x_+}+\boldsymbol\alpha_+)}{\mathrm{B}(\boldsymbol\alpha_+)}  </math>

where <math>\mathbf{x_+}</math> and <math>\boldsymbol\alpha_+</math> are the <math>m+1</math> dimensional vectors created by appending the scalars <math>x_0</math> and <math>\alpha_0</math> to the <math>m</math> dimensional vectors <math>\mathbf{x}</math> and <math>\boldsymbol\alpha</math>  respectively and <math>\mathrm{B}</math> is the multivariate version of the [[beta function]]. We can write this equation explicitly as

:<math>\Pr(\mathbf{x}\mid x_0, \alpha_0, \boldsymbol{\alpha})=x_0\frac{\Gamma(\sum_{i=0}^m x_i)\Gamma(\sum_{i=0}^m \alpha_i)}{\Gamma(\sum_{i=0}^m (x_i+\alpha_i))} \prod_{i=0}^m \frac{\Gamma(x_i+\alpha_i)}{\Gamma(x_i+1)\Gamma(\alpha_i)}.</math>

Alternative formulations exist. One convenient representation<ref>Farewell, Daniel & Farewell, Vernon. (2012). Dirichlet negative multinomial regression for overdispersed correlated count data. Biostatistics (Oxford, England). 14. 10.1093/biostatistics/kxs050.</ref> is

:<math>\Pr(\mathbf{x}\mid x_0, \alpha_0, \boldsymbol{\alpha})= \frac{\Gamma(x_\bullet)}{\Gamma(x_0)\prod_{i=1}^m \Gamma(x_i+1)} \times \frac{\Gamma(\alpha_\bullet)}{\prod_{i=0}^m \Gamma(\alpha_i)} \times \frac{\prod_{i=0}^m \Gamma(x_i+\alpha_i)}{\Gamma(x_\bullet+\alpha_\bullet)}</math>

where <math> x_\bullet= x_0+x_1+ \cdots + x_m </math> and <math> \alpha_{\bullet}= \alpha_0+\alpha_1+ \cdots + \alpha_m </math>.

This can also be written

:<math>\Pr(\mathbf{x}\mid x_0, \alpha_0, \boldsymbol{\alpha})=\frac{\mathrm{B}(x_\bullet,\alpha_\bullet)}{\mathrm{B}(x_0,\alpha_0)}\prod_{i=1}^m \frac{\Gamma(x_i+\alpha_i)}{x_i! \Gamma(\alpha_i)}.
</math>

==Properties==
===Marginal distributions===
To obtain the [[marginal distribution]] over a subset of Dirichlet negative multinomial random variables, one only needs to drop the irrelevant <math>\alpha_i</math>'s (the variables that one wants to marginalize out) from the <math>\boldsymbol{\alpha}</math> vector. The joint distribution of the remaining random variates is <math>\mathrm{DNM}(x_0,\alpha_0,\boldsymbol{\alpha_{(-)}})</math> where <math>\boldsymbol{\alpha_{(-)}}</math> is the vector with the removed <math>\alpha_i</math>'s. The univariate marginals are said to be [[beta negative binomial distribution|beta negative binomially]] distributed.

===Conditional distributions===

If ''m''-dimensional '''x''' is partitioned as follows
:<math>
\mathbf{x}
=
\begin{bmatrix}
 \mathbf{x}^{(1)} \\
 \mathbf{x}^{(2)}
\end{bmatrix}

\text{ with sizes }\begin{bmatrix} q \times 1 \\ (m-q) \times 1 \end{bmatrix}</math>
and accordingly  <math>\boldsymbol{\alpha}</math> 
:<math>
\boldsymbol\alpha
=
\begin{bmatrix}
 \boldsymbol\alpha^{(1)} \\
 \boldsymbol\alpha^{(2)}
\end{bmatrix}
\text{ with sizes }\begin{bmatrix} q \times 1 \\ (m-q) \times 1 \end{bmatrix}</math>
then the [[Conditional_probability_distribution|conditional distribution]] of <math>\mathbf{X}^{(1)}</math> on <math>\mathbf{X}^{(2)}=\mathbf{x}^{(2)}</math> is <math>\mathrm{DNM}(x_0^{\prime},\alpha_0^{\prime},\boldsymbol\alpha^{(1)}) </math> where
:<math>
x_0^{\prime} = x_0 + \sum_{i=1}^{m-q} x_i^{(2)}
</math>
and
:<math>
\alpha_0^{\prime} = \alpha_0 + \sum_{i=1}^{m-q} \alpha_i^{(2)}
</math>.

That is,

:<math>\Pr(\mathbf{x}^{(1)}\mid \mathbf{x}^{(2)}, x_0,  \alpha_0, \boldsymbol{\alpha})= \frac{\mathrm{B}(x_\bullet,\alpha_\bullet)}{\mathrm{B}(x_0^{\prime} ,\alpha_0^{\prime}) }\prod_{i=1}^q\frac{\Gamma(x_i^{(1)}+\alpha_i^{(1)})}{(x_i^{(1)}!)\Gamma(\alpha_i^{(1)})} </math>

====Conditional on the sum====
The conditional distribution of a Dirichlet negative multinomial distribution on <math>\sum_{i=1}^m x_i = n</math> is [[Dirichlet-multinomial distribution]] with parameters <math>n</math>  and <math>\boldsymbol{\alpha}</math>. That is

:<math>\Pr(\mathbf{x} \mid  \sum_{i=1}^m x_i =n, x_0, \alpha_0, \boldsymbol{\alpha})= \frac{n!\Gamma\left(\sum_{i=1}^m  \alpha_i\right)}
{\Gamma\left(n+\sum_{i=1}^m \alpha_i\right)}\prod_{i=1}^m\frac{\Gamma(x_{i}+\alpha_{i})}{x_{i}!\Gamma(\alpha_{i})} </math>.

Notice that the expression does not depend on <math>x_0</math> or <math>\alpha_0</math>.

===Aggregation===
If

:<math>X = (X_1, \ldots, X_m)\sim\operatorname{DNM}(x_0, \alpha_0, \alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_m)</math>

then, if the random variables with positive subscripts ''i'' and ''j'' are dropped from the vector and replaced by their sum,

:<math>X' = (X_1, \ldots, X_i + X_j, \ldots, X_m)\sim\operatorname{DNM} \left(x_0, \alpha_0, \alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_i+\alpha_j,\ldots,\alpha_m \right).</math>


===Correlation matrix===
For <math>\alpha_0>2</math> the entries of the [[Correlation matrix#Correlation matrices|correlation matrix]] are

:<math>\rho(X_i,X_i) = 1.</math>

:<math>\rho(X_i,X_j) = \frac{\operatorname{cov}(X_i,X_j)}{\sqrt{\operatorname{var}(X_i)\operatorname{var}(X_j)}} =   \sqrt{\frac{\alpha_i  \alpha_j}{(\alpha_0+\alpha_i-1)(\alpha_0+\alpha_j-1)}}.</math>

===Heavy tailed===
The Dirichlet negative multinomial is a [[heavy tailed distribution]]. It does not have a [[List_of_mathematical_jargon#finite|finite]] [[mean]] for <math>\alpha_0 \leq 1</math> and it has infinite [[covariance matrix]] for <math>\alpha_0 \leq 2</math>. Therefore the [[moment generating function]] does not exist.

== Applications ==
===Dirichlet negative multinomial as a Pólya urn model===

In the case when the <math>m+2</math> parameters <math>x_0,  \alpha_0</math> and <math>\boldsymbol{\alpha}</math> are positive integers the Dirichlet negative multinomial can also be motivated by an [[urn model]] - or more specifically a basic [[Pólya urn model]]. Consider an urn initially containing <math>\sum_{i=0}^m{\alpha_i} </math> balls of <math>m+1</math> various colors including <math>\alpha_0</math> red balls (the stopping color). The vector <math>\boldsymbol{\alpha}</math> gives the respective counts of the other balls of various <math>m</math> non-red colors. At each step of the model, a ball is drawn at random from the urn and replaced, along with one additional ball of the same color. The process is repeated over and over, until <math>x_0</math> red colored balls are drawn. The random vector <math>\mathbf{X}</math> of observed draws of the other <math>m</math> non-red colors are distributed according to a <math>\mathrm{DNM}(x_0, \alpha_0, \boldsymbol{\alpha})</math>. Note, at the end of the experiment, the urn always contains the fixed number <math>x_0+\alpha_0</math> of red balls while containing the random number <math>\mathbf{X}+\boldsymbol{\alpha}</math> of the other <math>m</math> colors.
